observations.title: G20 names five expected traces for the Cancel-linearization branches and none for the death-ordering branches introduced in the same version
observations.detail: $.g20.executes enumerates terminal-wins, Cancel-wins, write-fails, already-terminal/already-cancelled, no-in-band - a clean one-to-one mapping onto the four hostEventTransitionRelation outcomes. The onHostObservedProcessDeath branch added in this same version carries two normative ORDERING rules (J-3 drain to EOF then death appended last with no shutdown/cancel/kill; and drained-and-reaped death completing an active ladder's T-5 without restart) and no trace asserts either. 'no-in-band' asserts that no Cancel was sent, not the append ordering or the no-restart property.
observations.whyNotAFinding: Deliberately NOT filed as SHOULD-FIX. $.g20.namingStanding is NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED - the harness does not exist, DR-G20 authoring is owned elsewhere (D-086, file 08 line 354), and 'with expected traces:' reads as illustrative rather than exhaustive. The composition's death rules are fully specified, so a harness author has everything needed. v4 also went from zero named traces in v3 to five. Denying acceptance over how exhaustively a not-yet-authored harness enumerates traces would be a preference dressed as a defect.
observations.suggestion: When DR-G20 is actually authored, add a death-ordering trace (drain-then-death-last, and death-completes-T-5-without-restart) so the CSCV3-B1 rule has a regression guard.

CSCV3-B1 limb verifies against source. onHostObservedProcessDeath.ifNoLadderActive ('Perform CPC J-3 bounded channel drain to EOF, then append the death boundary event last') matches CPC v2's J-3 in substance word for word: 'All channels are drained to EOF - every octet read and delivered - before the death event is appended ... Death is therefore always the LAST event of a child's merged order.' I specifically tested the opposite hypothesis - that appending death last contradicts the mechanism's 'each event is appended at host observation' - and J-3 resolves it explicitly in the artifact's favour.

ifLadderAlreadyActive ('the drained and reaped death completes the active ladder's T-5 terminal step. Do not restart the ladder') matches J-5's ladder, whose T-5 is 'reap and final death event', and respects J-5's 'one-way ... never skips backward ... never truncates or rewrites the merged order retroactively'. Handling a spontaneous death under J-3 without starting a ladder is lawful: J-3 governs EOF/process death independently and states no precondition that a ladder be active.

CSCV3-B2 limb verifies against source. The linearization point is a behavioural property, not an API: it names atomic validate-and-commit-or-reject against concurrent provider terminal events, and explicitly disclaims choosing an SDK API - consistent with the DR-125 row's 'exact APIs/frameworks deferred'. ifNotAdmissible's coverage of already-terminal and already-cancelled states matches delivery.v2's cancelTransition ('Cancel may be sent once from any nonterminal state; only Cancelled may follow'), and the commit-first-then-teardown ordering matches delivery.v2's userCancellation sequence.

ifAdmissibleAndCommitFails is sound and mints nothing: it proceeds to CPC teardown, forbids inventing a Cancel that did not commit, forbids stalling teardown on a failed commit, and defers recording of the failure to the owning provider and CPC contracts rather than assigning it meaning here.

summary: I attacked every surface the dispatch and the artifact's own reviewGuidance name, and found no blocker and no SHOULD-FIX. The two repairs verify against primary sources rather than against the reviewers' framing: the death branch reproduces CPC v2's J-3 almost word for word ('Death is therefore always the LAST event of a child's merged order'), and I specifically tested the opposite hypothesis - that appending death last contradicts the merged order's append-at-observation rule - and found J-3 resolves it in the artifact's favour. The linearization point names required race-resolution behaviour without choosing an API, its not-admissible branch matches delivery.v2's nonterminal-state rule, and the commit-failure branch neither invents a frame nor stalls teardown. The closed roster is exact for the first time in the series, including both scoped sub-paths, and four of the six composition sub-keys are byte-identical to v3 text I had already cleared. My CLAUDE-V3-SF1 is repaired, and two of my v3 observations were folded unasked. The carried text remains byte-exact, every pin is live, and nothing mints a D-096 (A) grant, a SATISFIED token, or an implementation authorization. The one coverage point I found - G20 names traces for the Cancel branches but not for the death-ordering branches - I deliberately declined to file as a finding: the harness is NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED and the composition rules are complete, so filing it would be a preference dressed as a defect.
